clips.text: So why could a brain squeezed to one millimetre still score one hundred twenty-six?
A scan showed brain tissue squeezed into a thin sheet around a huge fluid chamber.
One Sheffield student still scored one hundred twenty-six and earned first-class honours in mathematics.
Another man held a civil-service job, married, and raised two children before doctors saw the scan.
His scan looked impossible beside the ordinary life he was already living.
So why could a brain squeezed to one millimetre still score one hundred twenty-six?
The fluid squeezed slowly for thirty years, and the thin layer learned to do the work. Tap the video link under my name.
